The APOA is now reflected in the LLDC resolution in a balanced way, capturing crucial elements from each of the 5 priority areas while maintaining balance between them. In particular, the EU notes that the ambitions of LLDCs related to trade are present in the resolution in the most comprehensive way possible. The EU also welcomes that the resolution addresses the issue of connectivity, both related to digital connectivity and sustainable infrastructure. The EU is especially pleased that the resolution, like the APOA, integrates language on both climate adaptation and mitigation. The holistic combination of mitigation efforts with adaptation strategies will enhance LLDC's resilience to the economic and climate crises. Partnerships are necessary for mobilizing means of implementation. Let me underscore that Team Europe has been committed to doing its part, including through investments in various projects such as the Lobito Corridor or the Team Europe Initiative on Water, Energy, and Climate in Central Asia, to name just 2 examples. Looking ahead, the EU hopes that the reports on major deliverables of the APOA, which this resolution remandates for the first session of the General Assembly will materialize in this new timeline.
